name: Epicure
description: Epicure gives Claude read-only access to a computational flavour model spanning 1,790 ingredients. Explore pairings, compare ingredients on sensory and cultural axes, discover substitutions and neighbours, locate ingredients on a flavour atlas, and navigate interpretable flavour transformations. Results are deterministic and computed from bundled model artefacts; Epicure does not call an external model.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Epicure to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Epicure to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://epicure-mcp.kaikaku.ai/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is Epicure MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of September 15, 2026, Epicure scores 100/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the Epicure MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Epicure lists 13 MCP tools, including closest_mode, compare_on_axis, cultural_profile, find_pairings, flavour_correlations, ingredient_on_factor, list_factors, list_targets, morph, neighbors, pairing_score, and pareto_navigate.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Epicure?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Epicure in data-analytics on the Manufact MCP catalog include Newsflash, Point Topic, Pricing Optimizer AI, StatCite, and ClickHouse Cloud MCP Server.
Epicure does not require authentication. It is a public MCP endpoint you can connect without logging in.
Epicure is developed by KAIKAKU.AI. It is listed as community on the Claude connector directory.
